What Tandem is

Tandem is pair development for a team of two — one human, one AI — over a git repository. You say what you want in your own words; the machine grounds it in the real code; you sign exactly what you saw; workers build it under verification you never have to take on faith; you accept the delivery by reading its proofs.

The shape

Everything moves through one surface (the space) and two decisions that are always yours:

  1. Sign — freezing a cut of grounded changes into a TEP. Nothing is built before this.

  2. Accept — merging a delivery whose proofs are green. Nothing lands after the build without this.

Between the gates the machine is autonomous, and it is not trusted: probes are written by workers that cannot see the implementation, completion is decided by a black-box oracle rather than a worker’s claim, files outside a worker’s declared footprint are reverted, and everything that could not be delivered is written on the delivery’s face.

The vocabulary

ask

Your words, kept verbatim. Everything derives from asks; asks are never machine-edited.

change

One grounded intention — a sentence, the file(s) it lands in, and the acceptance criteria that prove it.

unit

Changes clustered by code coupling; the thing you add to a cut.

cut

The set of changes you are about to freeze.

TEP

A signed cut — named TEP-<you>-<n>, bound by a cryptographic token to exactly what you saw when you signed.

slice

The engine’s dispatch unit inside a TEP: one coder, its held-out probe authors, a footprint.

delivery

A branch plus its proofs, offered for your accept.
